# 6. Cell visualization

**Module 06 — Cell visualization.** 
In this module, we will visualize 2D and 3D single-cell graph plots using
pixelatorR's `cell_plot` visualization framework. This shows *where* proteins sit on a
single cell's surface graph and can help visualize clustering, polarization and colocalization patterns. See the [cell visualization tutorial](https://software.pixelgen.com/pna-analysis/R/tutorials/cell_visualization/) for more detail.

```{r}
#| label: module06b_setup

library(here)
here::i_am("modules/06_cell_visualization.qmd")

source(here::here("modules", "common_setup.R"))

if (!exists("pg_data", inherits = TRUE)) {
  pg_data <- load_checkpoint("annotated_seurat_object.rds")
}
```

## 6.1. Parameters

> **Decision checkpoint**
> Set the cell type and markers to plot. In practice, cell visualization is an interactive process, where you select cells and markers of interest based on prior knowledge and/or analysis results and then plot them - often in multiple ways. 

As an example, we will visualize CD8 T cells and in particular the markers CD82 and CD81. This is a pair of proteins which often colocalize on the cell surface. 

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_parameters

cell_type_of_interest <- "CD8 T"           # one value from `cell_annotation`
markers_to_viz        <- c("CD82", "CD81") # pair inspected for colocalization
n_cells               <- 4                 # cells in the grid and the grid animation
# Grey background nodes, one color per marker in `markers_to_viz`
marker_colors <- c(Other = "grey85", CD82 = "#E53E3E", CD81 = "#3182BD")
light_direction <- c(-1, 0.5, 1)           # shared lighting for the static renders
out_dir <- here::here("results/06_cell_visualization")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## 6.2. Select cells

How you pick cells depends on what you want to show — the spatial pattern on typical cells, a
polarized marker, a colocalization pattern, or a cell–cell conjugate. In this example, we rank cells of the chosen type by the colocalization `log2_ratio` of the marker pair, and keep those with enough observed joins that the ratio is meaningful and interesting to visualize.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_select_cells

# Sample `n_cells` cells from the cells of interest
sel_cells <- pg_data |>
  subset(cell_annotation == cell_type_of_interest) |>
  ProximityScores(lazy = TRUE) |>
  filter(
    marker_1 %in% markers_to_viz,
    marker_2 %in% markers_to_viz,
    marker_1 != marker_2
  ) |>
  filter(join_count > 100) |>
  arrange(desc(log2_ratio)) |>
  collect() |>
  slice_head(n = n_cells)

cells_of_interest <- sel_cells$component
if (length(cells_of_interest) == 0) {
  stop("No '", cell_type_of_interest, "' cells pass the selection filter.")
}
```

Each figure below is its own pipeline. `RemoveCellGraphs()` drops graphs left by another chunk, `LoadCellGraphs()` reads only the cells that figure draws, and `ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral")` stores coordinates under the name `spectral_3d`. `ComputeLPS()` runs only when the color is a local proximity score. A counts plot or a marker-identity plot stops after the layout. The cell selection above is the only step these figures share, so the chunks can be run in any order. Each chunk repeats the load so it can be run on its own.

## 6.3. Single cell, marker counts

A 2D projection of one cell, colored by CD82 counts. This shows where the individual proteins sit. Depth and directional light make near and far nodes read as a surface without an interactive viewer. Counts live on the graph already, so this chunk does not compute local proximity scores.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_marker_counts

# Counts are already stored on the graph, so this figure does not score neighborhoods.
# markers_to_viz[1] is CD82 in the parameter block; the plot reads that column by name.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest[1]) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral")

layout_counts <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz[1],
  layer = "counts"
)

p_counts <- layout_counts |>
  cell_plot(color = CD82, size = 0.7) |>
  cell_node_depth(focal_distance = 1.8) |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction) |>
  cell_annotation(
    title = paste(cell_type_of_interest, "—", cells_of_interest[1]),
    legend_title = "CD82"
  )

export_plot(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_counts.png")),
  plot = autoplot(p_counts)
)
```

The same recipe can be opened as an interactive 3D view. `cell_plot_interactive()` keeps the colors and the layout from the chunk above. Drag to rotate and scroll to zoom. On a grid, the panels share one camera, so they turn together. The view can be embedded in an HTML report. This chunk is left unevaluated so rendering the report does not open a widget. Run the figure first, then run this chunk when you want the viewer. 

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_marker_counts_interactive
#| eval: false

p_counts |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```

## 6.4. Single cell, one local proximity score

The same cell, colored by the CD82 local proximity score. The count plot shows the molecules. This plot shows the neighborhood where those molecules cluster, including the nodes between them. The default `ComputeLPS()` call stores one self-clustering score per node per marker in the `lps` layer. Only CD82 is requested, because that is the only score this figure draws.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_marker_lps

# One marker, self-clustering only. Colocalization is not drawn here.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest[1]) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz[1])

layout_lps <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz[1],
  layer = "lps"
)

p_lps <- layout_lps |>
  cell_plot(color = CD82, size = 0.7) |>
  cell_node_scale_color() |>
  cell_node_depth(focal_distance = 1.8) |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction) |>
  cell_annotation(
    title = paste(cell_type_of_interest, "—", cells_of_interest[1]),
    legend_title = "CD82 LPS"
  )

export_plot(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_lps.png")),
  plot = autoplot(p_lps)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_marker_lps_interactive
#| eval: false

p_lps |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```

## 6.5. Single cell, multi-marker overlay

Several markers on the same cell. `FetchLayoutData(add_marker = TRUE)` adds the protein identity of each node from the counts matrix. Nodes for `markers_to_viz` keep their name, and every other node is labeled `"Other"`. Identity comes from the counts, so local proximity scores are not computed.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_multi_marker

# Marker identity is enough. The overlay does not color by a score.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest[1]) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral")

layout_counts <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  add_marker = TRUE,
  layer = "counts"
)

p_multi_marker <- layout_counts |>
  mutate(
    marker = if_else(marker %in% markers_to_viz, marker, "Other"),
    highlight = as.numeric(marker != "Other")
  ) |>
  cell_plot(color = marker, size = highlight, alpha = highlight) |>
  cell_node_scale_color(colors = marker_colors) |>
  cell_node_scale_size(sizes = c(0.4, 3)) |>
  cell_node_scale_alpha(alphas = c(0.5, 1))

export_plot(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_multi_marker.png")),
  plot = autoplot(p_multi_marker)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_multi_marker_interactive
#| eval: false

p_multi_marker |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```

## 6.6. Single cell, local proximity panels

Local proximity scores for each marker and for the pair, on one cell. The first `ComputeLPS()` stores self-clustering of each marker in the `lps` layer. The second call, with `mode = "all"`, stores one colocalization score per node in the node metadata under `coloc`. The two fetches walk the nodes in the same order, so binding `coloc` by position keeps each score on its node.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_cell_lps_panels

# Both score types are drawn: per-marker clustering and the pair colocalization.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest[1]) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz) |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz, mode = "all", name = "coloc")

layout_lps <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz,
  layer = "lps"
)
layout_coloc <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = "coloc"
)
# Same node order in both tables, so coloc stays on the node it was computed for.
layout_lps <- bind_cols(layout_lps, layout_coloc |> select(coloc))

p_lps_panels <- layout_lps |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(c(markers_to_viz, "coloc")),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  cell_plot(color = score, size = 0.6) |>
  cell_grid(cols = score_type) |>
  cell_node_scale_color() |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction)

export_plot(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_lps_panels.png")),
  plot = autoplot(p_lps_panels)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_single_cell_lps_panels_interactive
#| eval: false

p_lps_panels |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```

## 6.7. Multi-cell grid

The same scores across the selected cells. Columns are cells, rows are score types, and one color limit keeps a strong score in one cell comparable to the others. This chunk loads every selected cell, because each column is a different component.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_grid

# The grid draws clustering and colocalization, so both score calls below are required.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz) |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz, mode = "all", name = "coloc")

layout_lps <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest,
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz,
  layer = "lps"
)
layout_coloc <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest,
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = "coloc"
)
layout_lps <- bind_cols(layout_lps, layout_coloc |> select(coloc))

p_grid <- layout_lps |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(c(markers_to_viz, "coloc")),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  cell_plot(color = score, size = 0.6) |>
  cell_grid(cols = component, rows = score_type) |>
  # White at 0 so negative scores read blue and positive scores read red
  cell_node_scale_color(colors = c("blue", "white", "red"), limits = c(-1, 1)) |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction)

export_plot(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_grid.png")),
  plot = autoplot(p_grid)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_grid_interactive
#| eval: false

p_grid |>
  cell_plot_interactive()
```

## 6.8. Animations

`cell_coord_rotate()` describes the turn and `cell_plot_animate()` renders it. `lock_light = TRUE` keeps the highlight fixed to the viewer while the cell turns. These chunks are left unevaluated because writing the GIF is slow. Run them when you want the file.

This animation colors one cell by the pair colocalization score. Self-clustering is not drawn, so only the `mode = "all"` call is needed. The result is node metadata named `coloc`, which `FetchLayoutData()` reads without a layer.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_animate_single
#| eval: false

# The GIF colors coloc only, so skip the per-marker self-clustering call.
pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest[1]) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz, mode = "all", name = "coloc")

FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest[1],
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = "coloc"
) |>
  cell_plot(color = coloc, size = 0.7) |>
  cell_node_scale_color() |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction, lock_light = TRUE) |>
  cell_coord_rotate(axis = "y", max_degree = 360) |>
  cell_plot_animate(
    file = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_", cells_of_interest[1], "_rotation.gif")),
    frames = 120,
    fps = 20,
    width = 500,
    height = 500
  )
```

A grid uses a short boomerang motion so each panel moves a short distance around its own centroid instead of spinning through a full turn. The panels are the same scores as the static grid, so both `ComputeLPS()` calls run again inside this chunk.

```{r}
#| label: cell_viz_animate_grid
#| eval: false

pg_data <- pg_data |>
  RemoveCellGraphs() |>
  LoadCellGraphs(cells = cells_of_interest) |>
  ComputeLayout(layout_method = "spectral") |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz) |>
  ComputeLPS(markers = markers_to_viz, mode = "all", name = "coloc")

layout_lps <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest,
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = markers_to_viz,
  layer = "lps"
)
layout_coloc <- FetchLayoutData(
  pg_data,
  cells = cells_of_interest,
  layout_method = "spectral_3d",
  vars = "coloc"
)
layout_lps <- bind_cols(layout_lps, layout_coloc |> select(coloc))

layout_lps |>
  pivot_longer(
    all_of(c(markers_to_viz, "coloc")),
    names_to = "score_type",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  cell_plot(color = score, size = 0.6) |>
  cell_grid(cols = component, rows = score_type) |>
  cell_node_scale_color(colors = c("blue", "white", "red"), limits = c(-1, 1)) |>
  cell_illuminate(light_direction = light_direction) |>
  cell_coord_rotate(axis = "y", max_degree = 30) |>
  cell_plot_animate(
    file = file.path(out_dir, paste0(cell_type_of_interest, "_grid_rotation.gif")),
    frames = 30,
    fps = 15,
    boomerang = TRUE,
    width = 300 * length(cells_of_interest),
    height = 300 * (length(markers_to_viz) + 1)
  )
```
